summary: Watcher Names — end-to-end verification. BACKEND: `python -m pytest tests/test_family_unlink.py -q -p no:warnings -n 0` → 5/5 PASS in 10.0s (unlink×3 + new watcher-names×2). FRONTEND (390x844 mobile viewport, two isolated browser contexts on preview URL, MockSecurityAdapter): all 10 scripted assertions PASS after one client-side fix. RCA: The privacy egress allow-list in /app/frontend/src/domain/privacy.ts (ALLOWED_KEYS.family) did NOT include the new `guardian_name` field that /family/link now sends, so every link attempt threw an EgressViolation client-side and never hit the server — the whole Watcher Names feature was blocked at the client. Added `guardian_name` to the family allow-list (single-token addition, matches backend LinkRequest.guardian_name Pydantic field, no other keys touched) and restarted expo. Post-fix flow, in order: (0) two anonymous devices onboarded (onboarding-start-button → disclosure-accept-button); apollo.device.identity.v2 populated in each context (deviceId + token + expiresAt). (pre) B typed 'Sarah' in family-owner-name, entered A's family-pair-code in family-link-code, tapped family-link-button → toast 'Now watching Mum' visible. (1) A reloaded /family: watcher row family-watcher-<link_id> reads 'Sarah · Paired 9/8/2026 · Remove' (NOT 'A family member'). (2) B reloaded /family: row family-watch-<A_device_id> present, label line family-watch-label-<A_device_id> reads 'They see you as “Sarah”', rename button count = 0 (name matches). (3) B changed family-owner-name to 'Sarah (daughter)' → rename link family-watch-rename-<A_id> appears with text 'Use “Sarah (daughter)” instead' → tap → toast 'They'll now see your name on their phone.' visible → label line updates to 'They see you as “Sarah (daughter)”' → A's watcher row updates to 'Sarah (daughter) · Paired · Remove'. (4) Regression: A tapped family-watcher-remove-<link_id>; web confirm auto-accepted via page.on('dialog', d.accept) → 'No devices linked yet.' present, watcher row absent. (5) Context C onboarded fresh with EMPTY family-owner-name, linked to fresh code from A → A's watcher row shows 'A family member · Paired · Remove' (neutral label preserved). No React Native red-screens, no deprecated packages introduced, no other console errors observed.

integration_issues.issue: Client-side privacy allow-list ALLOWED_KEYS.family in src/domain/privacy.ts was missing 'guardian_name' — every link request threw EgressViolation and never left the device, breaking the entire Watcher Names feature. Fixed in this iteration (see updated_files). Root cause: privacy.ts wasn't updated alongside LinkRequest.guardian_name and the family.tsx link mutation.

action_items: Applied: added 'guardian_name' to ALLOWED_KEYS.family in /app/frontend/src/domain/privacy.ts. Confirm this addition is intended and covered by the privacy policy summary (it's the guardian's own display name — same category as owner_name and from_name, both of which are already allowed). If policy language needs updating, PRIVACY_POLICY_SUMMARY should mention that a paired watcher's chosen display name is stored server-side so the protected person's app can show it.

Optional test-infra addition: extend test_family_unlink.py::TestWatcherNames with a case where /api/family/link is called without guardian_name (empty) to lock in the 'A family member' neutral label — currently covered by test_pairing_without_a_name_keeps_the_neutral_label via the `pair(p,g)` helper which omits it, so this is already implicit.
critical_code_review_comments: backend routers/family.py:link_device (lines 161-172): correctly persists `guardian_label` only when body.guardian_name.strip() is truthy — the empty-name path keeps the neutral 'A family member' label via list_links line 222 default. Sound.

backend routers/family.py:rename_watcher (lines 180-190): authorises via {_id, guardian_device_id, deleted_at:None} so only the guardian side of the pairing can rename; protected user and strangers get 404 'Unknown pairing.' — verified in test_guardian_name_travels_with_the_pairing_and_can_be_changed. Pydantic min_length=1 gives 422 on empty rename. Good.

frontend/app/family.tsx: line 116 sends guardian_name in the link mutation and line 111 sends {name} for the rename mutation — both consistent with backend contract. Line 232 shows the 'Use “X” instead' rename link only when the typed owner value differs from l.my_label — clean UX for the 'name matches' case.

PRIMARY MISS (fixed by tester): /app/frontend/src/domain/privacy.ts ALLOWED_KEYS.family — must include 'guardian_name' or every /family/link call throws EgressViolation before hitting the network. This is a systemic pattern: any new field added to a backend endpoint that the client posts to also needs an allow-list entry here. Consider a comment above ALLOWED_KEYS.family enumerating the corresponding backend router paths.

frontend/app/family.tsx line 232: `owner.trim() && owner.trim() !== l.my_label` — correct dependency on the currently-typed family-owner-name; but note this hides the rename option if the guardian visits with a stale owner-name field. Acceptable for the MVP.

success_rate.frontend: 10/10 review flows PASS end-to-end after the privacy allow-list fix (pre-fix: 0/10 — every link was blocked client-side). Coverage: onboarding×3 contexts, pair-code creation, link with guardian_name='Sarah', A watcher shows Sarah, B label line + no rename button, rename to 'Sarah (daughter)' + toast + both sides update, Remove regression + confirm dialog + empty-state, empty-guardian-name pairing → 'A family member' neutral label.

seed_data_creation: Ephemeral only: 5 anonymous devices registered across the run (2 fresh for the failing pre-fix attempt + 3 fresh for the post-fix E2E). 3 pair codes generated, 2 successful links, 1 rename, 1 unlink, 1 empty-guardian-name link. All bound to short-lived anonymous device ids; no writes to seeded blocklist/admin data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Watcher Names is now fully wired: server stores per-pairing guardian_label via /family/link (guardian_name=…) and PUT /family/links/{id}/name (name=…); GET /family/links surfaces it as watchers[i].guardian_label (protected view) and i_watch[i].my_label (guardian view). The client picks up my_label to show 'They see you as “X”' and offers a rename link when the guardian's currently-typed owner-name differs. Empty guardian_name preserves the neutral 'A family member' label. Critical gotcha: any new field posted from the client MUST be listed in ALLOWED_KEYS.<endpoint> in /app/frontend/src/domain/privacy.ts — otherwise EgressViolation is thrown before the request leaves the device and the network tab shows nothing. Playwright notes: Playwright's page.screenshot() rejects `quality` for PNG paths (use .jpg or drop the arg); page.on('dialog', lambda d: asyncio.create_task(d.accept())) must be attached before clicking Remove/Stop. Two-context setup via `browser = page.context.browser; ctx = await browser.new_context(...)`. localStorage['apollo.device.identity.v2'] is a JSON string; sometimes it's double-encoded — parse defensively.
rca_of_issue: Symptom: tapping family-link-button rendered a red family-error banner 'Privacy policy blocked field “guardian_name” from leaving the device (family).' and no /api/family/link request was made. Root cause: /app/frontend/src/api/client.ts routes 'family' calls through enforceEgress() in /app/frontend/src/domain/privacy.ts, which validates every payload key against ALLOWED_KEYS.family (a whitelist). The new Watcher Names feature added a `guardian_name` field on the outbound /family/link body (family.tsx line 116) but the allow-list was NOT updated in the same commit. `enforceEgress` therefore threw EgressViolation for every attempt, and family.tsx surfaced it via `setErr(e.message)`. Fix: added 'guardian_name' to the family Set literal (single word). This matches backend Pydantic LinkRequest.guardian_name (routers/family.py line 138) which is already validated server-side (max_length=40, optional). Reproduction (pre-fix): Context B onboarded, /family, owner-name='Sarah', code=<valid>, tap Link → error visible, watcher never appears on A. Post-fix: 10/10 E2E checks pass.
